note: Deep-dive #10. Multi-pane captures in demo.md run in sequence in one terminal (kubectl watches end with --request-timeout). The portal counts are in the 'also' notes of each screen. Record the real replica count and say it in the narration if it is not ten.
prepare: # owner signs in (device code), not recorded
az login --use-device-code
dotnet test tests/FinanceReview.Tests -m:1
python -m pip install -q pytest PyYAML; python -m pytest tests/contracts -q
az extension add -n k8s-extension --only-show-errors
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.KubernetesConfiguration; az provider register --namespace Microsoft.ContainerService
az vm list-skus -l westeurope --size Standard_D2s_v5 -o table
az group create -n rg-mglab-deep-dive-10 -l westeurope -o none
az deployment group create -g rg-mglab-deep-dive-10 -n main -f infra/main.bicep --query properties.outputs -o json > outputs.json
$o = Get-Content outputs.json | ConvertFrom-Json
az aks get-credentials -g rg-mglab-deep-dive-10 -n $o.aksName.value --overwrite-existing
kubectl get nodes
az acr build -r $o.acrName.value -t finance-worker:1 src/FinanceReview.Worker
kubectl annotate serviceaccount keda-operator azure.workload.identity/client-id=$($o.kedaClientId.value) -n kube-system --overwrite; kubectl rollout restart deploy keda-operator -n kube-system

az role assignment create --role 'Azure Service Bus Data Sender' --assignee-object-id (az ad signed-in-user show --query id -o tsv) --assignee-principal-type User --scope (az servicebus topic show -g rg-mglab-deep-dive-10 --namespace-name $o.serviceBusNamespace.value -n purchase-events --query id -o tsv) -o none
Start-Sleep -Seconds 240   # role assignments can take a few minutes
python scripts/render_manifests.py --outputs outputs.json --image "$($o.acrLoginServer.value)/finance-worker:1" --out build
kubectl apply -f build/
kubectl rollout status deploy -n contoso-finance --timeout=300s
python scripts/send_burst.py --namespace $o.serviceBusNamespace.value --count 3   # dry run: a manual burst of 3 is processed
Start-Sleep -Seconds 200   # let KEDA scale the worker back to zero (cooldown 120 s)

screens.name: platform
commands: az aks show -g rg-mglab-deep-dive-10 -n $o.aksName.value --query "[workloadAutoScalerProfile, securityProfile, oidcIssuerProfile]" -o json | ForEach-Object { $_ -replace '"issuerURL": ".*"', '"issuerURL": "<masked>"' }
also: Issuer URL is replaced on screen by <masked>; subscription id and tenant id are not printed by these commands; blur the registry name if it shows

screens.name: idle
prepare: Start-Sleep -Seconds 150   # make sure the cooldown has passed with an empty subscription
also: Right-hand capture (browser, labadmin): portal > Service Bus > purchase-events > Subscriptions > finance-review, active message count 0. Mask the namespace name and subscription id.

screens.name: scale-out
also: The first watch shows pods going from 0 to several Running while the sixty valid messages are handled (1.5 s each per handler); the second watch, started about two minutes after the last message, shows pods Terminating back to zero. State the real replica count in the narration.
Third capture (browser): portal finance-review active count falling to 0 (refresh), run alongside the first watch.

screens.name: logs
also: Expect 'Finance review opened for PR-90xx' lines from several pods and two 'Delivery DROP' warnings. Then portal (browser): finance-review active 0 and dead-letter 0. Record right after the burst, before the pods are gone, or the logs of terminated pods are lost.

teardown: kubectl config delete-context aks-mgl10; kubectl config delete-cluster aks-mgl10
needs: paid:AKS 2 x Standard_D2s_v5 nodes per hour, Service Bus Standard, ACR Basic (delete same day)
